exposure: Bladder-first approach (upfront dissection of uterovesical space) during cesarean hysterectomy
outcome: Neonatal outcome (live-born neonates, Apgar score, NICU care, neonatal death)
cohort: 78 women with placenta accreta spectrum disorder who underwent cesarean hysterectomy using the 'bladder-first approach'.
finding: The upfront dissection of the uterovesical space or 'bladder-first approach' during cesarean hysterectomy for placenta accreta spectrum disorder was found to reduce hemorrhage and bladder injury, with no adverse effect on neonatal outcome.
mod_finding: The bladder-first approach, a specific surgical technique during cesarean hysterectomy (a mode of birth), was found to reduce hemorrhage and bladder injury without negatively impacting neonatal outcomes.
followup_time: Up to 3 days postpartum (for neonatal death); until hospital discharge for mothers (not specified length).
